title: GH#36000: fix(pulse): make draft checkpoint cooldown take effect across cycles (GH#36000)
body:
## Summary

Resolves #36000 (t18795).

- Attribute checkpoint continuation verdicts to the issue for production log filtering.
- Never cool transient continuation launch failures.
- Extend quiet, unassigned checkpoint records to six hours, preserving revision/label invalidation and base disable behavior.

Files: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh`.
Reference: existing checkpoint negative-cache reader and candidate log filter.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: medium. Testing level: runtime-verified.

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh` — PASS
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` — PASS
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh` — PASS
- `shellcheck` on all four changed scripts — PASS
- `git diff --check` — PASS

The pre-push hook reports `bun run typecheck` cannot start because this runner has no installed TypeScript dev dependencies (`tsc: command not found`); the existing CI typecheck owns that unrelated check. This shell-only change does not alter Node/TypeScript files.

## Acceptance self-review

| Criterion | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Helper verdicts reach the issue-specific reader and record cooldown | Real attention emitter plus production LOGFILE reader; realistic no-stall and capability-release verdicts; issue-prefix and repo isolation |
| Quiet unassigned records survive base TTL | One-hour-old record remains filtered with default six-hour quiet TTL |
| Recent or assigned records keep base expiry | 14399/14400-second write-time horizon boundary and assigned snapshot coverage |
| Disable and invalidation preserved | Base zero, quiet zero, revision/label edits, label-order invariance, invalid-setting fallback, one-day cap |
| Transient launch windows never cool | Launch-failure log windows and preserved older PR-fingerprinted block |
| Other reasons unchanged | Existing runner-capability and PR-fingerprint paths remain independent; only checkpoint-cooldown branch selects quiet TTL |

No deployment or release was authorized. After deployment, the operational owner can verify checkpoint-skip log entries across cycles and reduced failed candidate-stage time; this PR does not claim those production metrics.

title: GH#36005: fix: close stale-reset never-ready claims and ready attempt rebinds in checkpoint history
body:
## Summary

Resolves #36005.

A preserved draft checkpoint could not get approved after later dispatch episodes had fully released. `approval-template` returned `intervening coordination is not fully released`. A read-only replay found two framework causes:

1. **Producer bug (manual dispatch).** `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` never allocated an attempt ID. Its prelaunch lease used whatever `AIDEVOPS_ATTEMPT_ID` the caller had, and the worker argv left the ID out. Since GH#35295 the worker runs in a managed `systemd-run --user` unit, which doesn't inherit the caller's environment, so the worker created a fresh ID before its ready lease. Pulse dispatch was never affected: `_dlw_begin_prelaunch` passes one ID in argv.
   - Fix: allocate one `attempt:` ID per dispatch (`_dsi_ensure_attempt_id`), pass it to the prelaunch transition and in the worker argv, and drop any inherited `AIDEVOPS_ATTEMPT_STARTED_AT`.
2. **History rejected two legitimate closures** (`pr_checkpoint_history.py`):
   - A claim that never reached ready, released by its owner's stale recovery (`reason=stale_assignment_reset`). This now closes as `outcome: stale_reset_before_ready`, under every `blocked_before_ready` guard plus a mandatory device match with the claim.
   - Prelaunch→ready attempt rotation (historical records from bug 1). History now accepts exactly one rebind at the first ready lease. It must come before any launch or release, on the claim's lease token, session and device. Later leases, launches and releases must match the rebound attempt.

Both remain explicit `released_successors` entries that a new approval must acknowledge; neither grants continuation by itself.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`: attempt allocation and propagation.
- `.agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_history.py`: `close_stale_reset_before_ready`, `lease_attempt_accepted`, claim device recorded in episode state (not emitted).
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-claim-only.py`: positive and fail-closed cases (wrong or missing device, live renewal, ready, launch, foreign actor, edit, unbound attempt; rebind after launch, second rebind, foreign device, terminal or release naming the prelaunch attempt, prelaunch-phase rebind, unprefixed ID).
- `.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md`: documents both closures.

## Verification

- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-claim-only.py`: 13 tests OK (4 new).
- `test-pr-checkpoint-revision.py` (19 OK), `test-pr-checkpoint-private-member.py` (5 OK), `test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` (120 passed), `test-dispatch-single-issue-prelaunch.sh` and `test-dispatch-single-issue-tracking.sh` pass.
- `test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`: 97/98. The one failure ("fresh runner capabilities block … checkpoint resume") reproduces identically on unmodified `main` scripts (managed lifetime evidence unavailable on macOS). It predates this PR and is unrelated.
- ShellCheck clean. Pre-commit ratchets pass.
- Read-only replay of the observed private checkpoint history (5 intervening episodes):
  - Unmodified code: `released_successor_history` returns `None`.
  - With this branch: the stale-reset episode and all three rotated-attempt episodes close.
  - With this branch plus #35513's unprefixed-ID normalisation (simulated in a temporary copy): all 5 episodes reconstruct.

## Relationship to #35513

The remaining episode in the observed history uses an unprefixed legacy attempt ID, which #35513 normalises. #35513 is based on an older `main` (`events()` signature differs) and will need a rebase. This PR does not depend on it.

title: GH#35968: detect alternating and non-progressing tool-call loops in continuation guard
body:
## Summary

Replaces the single previous-failure fingerprint with a bounded per-session window (new session-continuation-loops.mjs). Detects cycles of period 1-4: failing cycles repeated threshold times save the existing recovery checkpoint and correction (named by tool cycle); all-success cycles repeated threshold+2 times with identical output only steer, never checkpoint, so they cannot block completion. Only progress (a new edit fingerprint, or a TodoWrite content/status change) resets the window; plain successes no longer clear it. aidevops_bounded_operation status/output polling is exempt. Documented in reference/session.md. The Critical risk classification comes from the word session in the module names; no auth/login session code is touched.



## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-continuation-guard.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-continuation-loops.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-session-continuation-checkpoint-helper.mjs, .agents/reference/session.md

## Decisions

Success-only cycles require identical output and two extra repetitions to avoid false positives on polling with changing output, and they steer only. Signals are deduplicated per rotation-independent cycle signature until progress resets the window.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — runtime-verified: drove the production guard through the same beforeTool/afterTool calls quality-hooks.mjs makes, with OpenCode-shaped bash outputs (metadata.exit 1). Before (main): 20 alternating A/B failures produced 0 replans. After: replan fires once at call 6 and appends the recovery correction to the tool output. node tests/test-session-continuation-checkpoint-helper.mjs passes new cases (identical failures at 3, A/B failures once at 6, fail/success alternation, identical success A/B at 10 with no checkpoint and no completion block, changing-output polling, reads+new edits, edit/todo resets, re-applied edits, bounded-operation polling). Full plugin suite npm --prefix .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops test exit 0; linters-local.sh --changed passes.

Resolves #35968

title: t18798: fix(plugin): stop denying all compound shell commands in every session (v3.39.87 regression)
body:
## Summary

f26477fca (GH#35978) moved the opaque-shell and interpreter -c denials in assertShellRead above the bound-session / empty-roots exemption. assertPrivateProcessingRead runs on every tool call, so since v3.39.87 every session (including sessions with no local-only roots) has every pipe, &&, ;, $VAR, glob and sh -c command denied with unclassifiable_shell_read. Headless workers stop at their first compound command and are released as permission_required, which waits for a maintainer retry. This keeps GH#35978's protections (literal operands are still canonically resolved before any exemption) and scopes the fail-closed denial: in bound or unclassified sessions, opaque text and -c scripts are denied only when they name a protected operator-config file (case-insensitive). Classified unbound sessions keep the strict literal-reader path.



## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/private-processing-policy.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-private-processing-policy.mjs, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t18798-brief.md

## Decisions

Opaque shell text cannot be classified exactly; denying all of it in every session breaks normal operation. Matching protected config basenames in opaque text keeps the GH#35978 alias protection with negligible false positives. Classified unbound sessions are unchanged.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Probe against the deployed v3.39.87 module with no roots and an unbound session: `git status && git log -1 | head -5` and `sh -c 'git status'` were denied (unclassifiable_shell_read), matching the worker blocker. With this change both are allowed, and `cat local-only-roots.json | wc` is still denied. test-private-processing-policy.mjs: 9/9 pass, including every GH#35978 alias, symlink and interpreter assertion and a new GH#36017 regression test. Full plugin suite (node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/) exits 0.

Resolves #36017

title: GH#36019: t18799 fix(pulse): continue open worker drafts after draft-checkpoint, clean and completed releases
body:
## Summary

Open worker drafts were held silently after worker_draft_checkpoint, clean and worker_complete releases: dispatch-stalled ignored those reasons, blocked-attention only covered clean/worker_complete, and closing-linked drafts were projected status:blocked so the continuation target fence rejected them. title: t18800: fix(pulse): restore stranded worker draft checkpoints
body:
## Summary

Runners before v3.39.89 projected `status:blocked` after a `clean`/`worker_complete` release while the worker's draft PR stayed open. The dispatch candidate filter skips `status:blocked` and the stale-blocked sweep resolves only dependency blocks, so those drafts were never continued, merged or surfaced. GH#36019 fixed the projection; this PR recovers issues already stranded (and any an un-updated runner strands). Live examples: #35977 (PR #35984), #35918 (PR #35928), #35592 (PR #35598).

`pulse-draft-checkpoint-unblock.sh` runs as a pass on the per-repo stale-blocked cadence with its own stamp (`draft-checkpoint-unblock-complete`). It restores `status:available` (releasing only the runner's assignment) only when trusted evidence proves the block was that projection:

- open `auto-dispatch` issue whose only status is `status:blocked`, with no protective label;
- exactly one open `origin:worker` draft closing it, targeting the repository default branch (GitHub honours closing keywords only there);
- newest trusted `CLAIM_RELEASED` is unedited, posted by the runner it names, with a continuable reason (not `blocked`, policy timeouts or `worker_ownership_lost`), and no later claim, dispatch or non-terminal lease (the attempt's own terminal lease is ignored, GH#33839);
- newest `labeled status:blocked` event is that runner's within the release window (−60 s/+600 s); a later maintainer re-block wins;
- assignees are only that runner; no audit marker for that release; under the per-PR cap (3).

One audit comment per restore and one `draft-checkpoint-unblock:` Pulse log line per decision, including the failing stage for unreadable listings, comments or timelines. Pulse then routes the draft through the existing `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT` → `dispatch-stalled` exact-head continuation or attention path. Drafts are never closed.

## History

The worker commit `2f3b7953ee` (dispatched for #36028) is preserved. An interactive session implemented the same brief in parallel (its claim was skipped while REST core was exhausted) and continued this branch with a merge (`9c5edb359b`). Review of the worker version found two defects, both verified:

1. Its ownership fence took the newest coordination event of any kind, so a release followed by the attempt's own `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=terminal` (common: #35977 18:58:19→18:58:42; #36028 03:47:43→03:47:57) was silently skipped.
2. It passed the paginated timeline with `jq --argjson`; #35592's timeline is 149,244 bytes, above Linux's 131,072-byte per-argument limit, so on Linux runners that issue would fail the whole pass every cycle.

The resolution keeps the interactive module (stdin-piped evidence, full pagination, per-issue failure isolation, `auto-dispatch` requirement) and adopts the worker's unedited-release and poster-equals-runner checks, its reason-set sync check and its real cadence-stamp tests. CodeRabbit's stage-logging finding was applied (`5a12c506c9`), and the worker then added the default-branch target guard (`29d90e899d`). The claim gap that allowed the parallel run is tracked as #36036.

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-draft-checkpoint-unblock.sh (new), .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-draft-checkpoint-unblock.sh (new), .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh (source module), .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh (pass + stamp via `_pulse_stale_blocked_optional_pass`), .agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md, TODO.md (t18800 entry; t18801 follow-up backlog entry)

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium — new label writes are gated on correlated trusted release and label-timeline evidence; every unreadable or ambiguous read means no write.
- **Verification:** `test-pulse-draft-checkpoint-unblock.sh` 57/57 at `29d90e899d` (including the large-timeline, terminal-lease, default-branch and stage-logging regressions and real cadence stamps). Sibling suites pass: `test-pulse-stale-blocked-reconcile.sh`, `test-pulse-graphql-budget-priority.sh`, `test-maintenance-selector-contract.sh`, `test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`. ShellCheck clean; `complexity-regression-helper.sh` bash32-compat/nesting-depth/file-size/function-complexity: 0 new. Live read-only dry run against marcusquinn/aidevops (writes stubbed, labels confirmed unchanged afterwards): selects exactly #35977, #35918 and #35592 and none of the other 11 blocked issues.

Resolves #36028

body:
## Summary

Resolves #36032.

- Preserve termination-cause reporting and per-operation TERM grace already merged in #35835 (0937ed7f5).
- Expose the existing 900-second default and 24-hour clamp, effective budget receipt, plugin/session/host lifetime limits, progress protocol, and 0.5-second default TERM grace in the native tool description.
- Document that the bounded manager/supervisor has no separate two-hour or idle timeout.
- Add one focused case to the existing lifecycle suite using its injected manager clock/timer and real supervisor path.

## Files and reference pattern

Files: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-tool.mjs`, `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/bounded-operation-termination-cases.mjs`, `.agents/reference/context-efficient-output.md`. No process containment, timeout policy, credentials or security controls changed.

## Runtime Testing

Runtime-verified on pushed head `3f102cb655046fce0c62ba46cb1aa786708e853a`, Node v22.23.3 (declared engine >=20).

```bash
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-operation-dispatch-launcher.mjs
node --check .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-tool.mjs
node --check .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/bounded-operation-termination-cases.mjs
git diff --check
```

32/32 tests passed, 49.1 seconds. The new test verifies both 86,400-second and oversized requests produce an 86,400,000-ms timer/receipt; after advancing only the manager clock to 7,216 seconds, status is still running with 79,184,000 ms remaining, no progress and no termination cause. The command then succeeds through the real supervisor. This is NOT a real two-hour soak.

Also exercised the existing native tool with budget_seconds=14400, kill_grace_seconds=60 and a Bash TERM trap that sleeps 30 seconds. After observing handler-ready, cancelled it: terminal state cancelled, termination_cause=cancel, process_exit=0, process_signal=null; captured output contains TERM received followed by cleaned. This runtime check exercises the already-deployed #35835 grace implementation, not a newly changed supervisor.

Local static-tool availability: markdownlint-cli2, biome and qlty are not on PATH. Existing code-quality.yml markdownlint/biome jobs and Qlty cover these checks. Unchanged pre-push hooks passed and explicitly deferred typecheck to CI because local tsc dependencies are absent; no root typecheck pass is claimed.

## Acceptance and review

Direct diff/self-review: only the tool description, six documentation lines and one focused existing-suite case changed; no lifecycle implementation was rewritten.

| Criterion | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Explicit effective budget and maximum | Tool/reference describe existing 24-hour clamp; regression verifies exact timer/receipt |
| Overdue output/progress does not impose two-hour cutoff | Manager-clock regression at 7,216 seconds; supervisor/manager source has only budget/lifecycle termination paths |

| Cause in status | Existing distinct-cause regressions pass; native cancellation receipt reports cancel |
| Historical sender | Unknown; no historical attribution or real two-hour soak claimed |

The budget is not a durable scheduler guarantee. Plugin reload/disposal, deleted sessions, host shutdown or external signals can still stop operations. Restart OpenCode after deployment to load the updated tool description.

title: t18804: attribute REST quota drain by auth and reset series
body:
## Summary

For #36048 / t18804. Preserve credential digest and response reset epoch as trailing v2 telemetry fields, and report REST-core remaining drops minus logged costs by independent auth/reset series and minute, with ranked burst minutes.

## Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh-api-instrument.sh`: append validated metadata without changing existing columns.
- `.agents/scripts/gh-quota-attribution-lib.sh`: carry existing header reset and credential digest into attempt rows.
- `.agents/scripts/gh-api-aggregate.awk`: replay separate series; exclude duplicates and missing metadata; expose attribution uncertainty.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-api-instrument.sh`: interleaved-pool, reset, legacy, duplicate and metadata regression checks.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-api-instrument.sh`: **257 passed, 0 failed**. Existing shim and SIGKILL fixtures now resolve installed utilities instead of assuming standard system binary locations; no production gate was relaxed.
- ShellCheck 0.11.0 on all three touched shell scripts: zero findings. The default wrapper could not find the binary, but the second executable reported by shell discovery worked.
- `git diff --check` and Bash syntax checks passed.
- Pre-push verification defers the repository-wide TypeScript check to existing CI because `tsc`/JavaScript dev dependencies are absent. No TypeScript or dependency files changed.

## Runtime Testing

`runtime-verified`: three real read-only REST requests through the worktree's exact-capture transport. Three attempt rows carried the same valid credential digest and reset epoch, with no missing metadata or counter increases. The aggregate reported remaining-drop 6, logged interval-owned cost 2, and unattributed cost 4. The first observation is a baseline; its request cost is intentionally outside the measured interval.

## Live investigation and remaining acceptance

**This PR completes the instrumentation, not the entire parent investigation. Keep #36048 open.** No closing keyword is used.

- Live probe window: epochs **1793340867–1793340869**, reset **1793343543**, remaining **2781 → 2777 → 2775**. Minute **1793340840** owns the four-unit residual.
- A simultaneous existing global row was labeled `gh_api_rest`, remaining **14406**, cost **1**. Its missing fingerprint/reset prevents associating it with the probe's series; merging those counters would be wrong.
- The retained global log had **2,682 REST-core attempts** in the sampled preceding hour, with **zero rows containing both new series fields** before the probe. Historical mixed counters cannot establish a majority consumer.
- A bounded 20-second process sample observed ten curl processes parented by the runner autoscaler, three by the app-token helper, and two native gh API processes parented by Bash. These are candidates only: process presence proves neither shared authentication nor quota cost. No credential values or arbitrary argv were retained in public evidence.
- The repository audit for Homebrew/local absolute gh paths found only native transport resolution and test cases, not a proven bypassing caller.

The unresolved parent acceptance remains: capture an instrumented burst on the affected runtime/fleet, bind the majority consumer to its pool, then fix or file its narrow fix and verify a reduced residual in a later comparable window. This run does **not** claim that identification or reduction.

## Compatibility and decisions

- Fields 1–19 and schema version 2 remain unchanged; new columns 20/21 are validated digest/reset fields. Older rows still parse but are explicitly excluded from pool-series attribution.
- Duplicate attempts are excluded. Independent resets do not create negative or merged drops. First samples establish baselines; incomplete costs and shared-user tokens make residuals upper bounds.
- Capture timestamps survive delayed appends after credential-lock release. Multi-frame rows use command-completion sample time, not falsely precise HTTP wall-clock times. Minute allocation is explicitly interval-ending-sample.
- No global deployment, credential change, publication, or speculative consumer remediation was performed.

body:
## Summary

For #36054 (t18804). Partial instrumentation delivery only; **do not close the issue**. Majority-consumer attribution and a later comparable reduction window remain unverified.

- Preserve response-owned cumulative `x-ratelimit-used` in optional trailing v2 field 22, after the existing fingerprint/reset fields.
- Carry the counter through per-response capture and deferred append, including zero-cost quota-state bootstrap. Unknown and nonnumeric values stay empty; cumulative used is never substituted for request cost.
- Keep sample time captured under the credential lock, independent auth/reset series, existing readers and zero-cost response handling unchanged.
- Modified files: `.agents/scripts/gh-api-instrument.sh`, `.agents/scripts/gh-quota-attribution-lib.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-api-instrument.sh`.

## Investigation

The current `.agents/scripts/gh` routes passthrough commands through `_shim_run_transport`; read rewrites invoke its instrumented `gh()` boundary. `.agents/scripts/github_auth_runtime.py` invokes the sibling shim with a recursion marker, not its own paginated/retried HTTP client. A scoped search of `.agents/` finds absolute native gh paths only in transport resolution and policy tests. These facts establish routing, not the historical majority consumer.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-api-instrument.sh`: 265 assertions passed, 0 failed, including old rows, interleaved series, capture time, per-page/retry counters, conditional zero costs and new used-counter propagation/validation.
- Separate `bash -n` invocations for all three modified scripts and `git diff --check`: passed.
- ShellCheck is unavailable locally: its installed wrapper cannot locate the real binary. CI coverage: `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`, `cross-platform-shellcheck`. No lint success is claimed here.
- Pre-push `bun run typecheck` could not start (`tsc` unavailable; worktree dependencies absent). The repository hook explicitly deferred it to CI and allowed the push. No dependency installation or gate bypass was performed.

## Runtime Testing

Runtime-verified instrumentation using native gh 2.102.0 and Bash 5.3.9: five read-only commands through the worktree shim with exact capture enabled (`api user`, `issue list`, `pr list`, `run list`, `release view`). All observed response frames retained numeric used/remaining/reset metadata; run-list produced two distinct response attempt rows. Issue/PR lists used GraphQL; run-list and release-view used REST. No full-host deployment or process pause was performed.

Live receipt, 2026-10-30 07:17:10–07:17:15Z (epochs 1793344630–1793344635), one non-secret credential digest:

| reset epoch | sampled used/remaining | observed REST drop | interval-owned logged cost | residual upper bound |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1793347144 | 2172/2828 → 2173/2827 → 2177/2823 | 5 | 2 | 3 |
| 1793347555 | 254/4746 → 255/4745 | 1 | 1 | 0 |

The separate reset series were not merged despite the same credential fingerprint. These tiny controlled intervals validate propagation and replay only; they **do not** identify the majority consumer or demonstrate a comparable post-fix reduction.

## Remaining investigation / runner limitation

The runner authenticates as `alex-solovyev`, not the original reporting user's credential context. The worker cannot invent historical provenance or authorize weakening protection of dependency/maintainer holds. Current same-second fixtures prove only heuristic behavior, not ownership.

title: t18808: fix(pulse): re-arm aged checkpoint attention for untried runners; take over idle interactive PRs after 12h
body:
## Summary

Worker draft checkpoints and idle interactive PRs no longer stall forever waiting for a human.

- **Checkpoint attention re-arm** (`pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`): a per-head `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION` / `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION` record now pauses the head instead of stopping it permanently. Once the newest attention record for the head is older than `AIDEVOPS_PCC_ATTENTION_REARM_SECONDS` (default 43200 = 12h, `0` restores the permanent stop), a runner that authored no claim, lease, launch or release after the head commit logs `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_REARMED` and makes one exact-head continuation through the existing `_pcc_dispatch` fence. Runners that already tried the head stay paused. The per-PR fuse (`AIDEVOPS_PCC_MAX_PR_RELEASES`) stays a hard stop, and protective labels, issue eligibility and the revision-bound approval for genuine `blocked` releases are unchanged.
- **Interactive handover** (`pulse-merge-conflict.sh`): `AIDEVOPS_INTERACTIVE_PR_HANDOVER_MODE` defaults to `enforce` and the idle threshold to 43200s (12h), per the maintainer decision. `no-takeover`, live claim stamps and active `status:*` labels still keep the PR with the human.
- The stall attention text now says the head is paused and when it re-arms. Docs: `reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md`, `reference/session.md`, `reference/override-flags.md`; diagnose pattern text updated.

## Root cause

`_pcc_dispatch_stalled` returned `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION_EXISTS` every Pulse cycle once `stalls >= 2` and a record existed, while `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT` held ordinary redispatch. A capability-limited runner's release plus one `worker_complete` continuation therefore froze the head for every runner, including runners that never tried it. The older `issue_metadata_ineligible` rejections on #35928 predate GH#35883; the current hold is this bound.

## Evidence

Live dry-run with this branch's helper against current GitHub state (runner `marcusquinn`, no dispatch):

```text
PR #35984 issue #35977 evidence=[...|worker_complete|2|true|2|false|...] tried=no  window=open
PR #35928 issue #35918 evidence=[...|worker_complete|2|true|2|false|...] tried=no  window=open
PR #35603 issue #35600 evidence=[...|worker_complete|2|true|2|false|...] tried=yes window=open
PR #35598 issue #35592 evidence=[...|worker_complete|2|true|2|false|...] tried=no  window=open
```

Three held drafts become continuable on this runner; #35603 stays paused here because this runner already tried that head.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`: 139 passed (new cases: aged re-arm for an untried runner, no re-arm for runners that tried the head, participation is head-scoped and fails closed, `0` disables, fuse is never re-armed).
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-interactive-handover.sh`: 18 passed (L3 now asserts the 12h/enforce defaults).
- `test-pulse-merge-pr-context.sh` (24), `test-pulse-merge-origin-interactive-auto-merge.sh` (12), `test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh` (39): all pass.
- `shellcheck` clean on changed scripts; `git diff --check` clean.

## Follow-up

The `origin:interactive` draft #35518 has no linked issue, so neither handover nor continuation can route it. It will be filed as a separate worker-ready issue.

Resolves #36077

title: fix(runtime): preserve PR-less completion rejection evidence (GH#36100)
body:
## Summary

Resolves #36100.

- Preserve bounded internal predicate names when PR-less objective proof is rejected, without changing completion acceptance or ownership checks.
- Carry the reason through existing classification source/pattern fields into exit diagnostics and metrics.
- Candidate discovery and scoped receipt verification remain separate; closed issues and model prose are not delivery proof.

## Files and reference pattern

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh`: fixed internal predicate names in `_hrw_pr_less_terminal_complete`, candidate discovery, scoped-receipt validation, and unpublished-work guards.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-result.sh`: retain the reason as `classification_source=pr_less_completion_rejected` and `classification_pattern=<predicate>` while keeping `premature_exit` and continuation behavior unchanged.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-completion-tests.sh`: 14 synthetic evidence shapes through the actual attempt/result/diagnostic/metric chain. Direct execution now invokes the existing parent harness instead of silently running no tests.

## Investigation result

The modeled older-PR case is rejected at `no_merged_pr_candidate` when the search for the newer issue number yields no candidate: scoped verification is never invoked. title: GH#36054: fix(gh): attribute auth-hop gh calls and make post-merge scanner quota-aware
body:
## Summary

For #36054 (t18804). Partial delivery: **do not close the issue**. This removes the attribution blind spot that the live 08:04–08:11Z window pointed at, and stops one deferrable consumer from draining search and REST-core quota. Closeout still requires a later comparable window showing a lower unattributed share.

### 1. Auth-hop caller attribution (`gh-native-transport-lib.sh`)

- Root cause: Pulse repository auth re-enters the shim via `python3 github_auth_runtime.py exec-gh <shim> ...`. The shim's parent process is therefore the Python resolver, not the framework script that issued the call. The bounded caller walk only skipped transparent wrappers (`timeout`, `env`, ...), so it stopped at the resolver and logged the attempt under the generic `gh_api_rest` label.
- Fix: `_shim_is_auth_runtime_hop` recognises exactly `python|python3|python3.*|Python [-flags] [path/]github_auth_runtime.py exec-gh` and lets the existing bounded walk (direct parent + at most two hops) continue past it. Unrelated Python processes remain unattributed rather than misattributed.

### 2. Quota-aware post-merge review scanner (`post-merge-review-scanner.sh`)

- Root cause: `issue_exists` ran one `gh issue list --search` per merged PR. Search allows 30 requests/minute, so each scan exhausted the search budget and starved other search consumers. During cooldowns the scanner kept going: uncertain lookups were skipped, so those PRs were not revisited until the next scanner interval.
- Fix:
  - Build one paginated REST issue index per scan (`issues?labels=...&state=all&since=<lookback>`). This is complete because the scan only lists PRs merged after the lookback date, and their follow-up issues are created after the merge. Malformed rows fail closed to the per-PR lookup. Post-claim rechecks stay fresh, because another runner may create the issue after the index was built.
  - Yield with the cursor preserved (`scanner_yield_at`) during a secondary cooldown, primary exhaustion of `core`/`graphql`/`search`, or when the Pulse REST-core priority budget defers deferrable work. An uncertain per-PR outcome that coincides with a cooldown returns a yield status (`SCANNER_PR_YIELD_RC=3`), so that PR is retried rather than skipped.
- `pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh rest-core-allows <class> <consumer>` exposes the existing priority-budget decision. `pulse-simplification-review.sh` enables it for the Pulse-launched scan (`SCANNER_REST_CORE_GATE=1`); manual runs are ungated.
- `shared-gh-primary-cooldown.sh` adds the resource-specific `_gh_primary_cooldown_active <resource>` probe.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-api-instrument.sh`: 266 passed, 0 failed. Includes a new regression for a real `python3 github_auth_runtime.py exec-gh` hop attributed to the calling script.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-post-merge-review-scanner.sh`: all passed. New cases cover the index, the PR #10 vs #101/#1010 boundary, malformed-row fallback, no search requests on indexed lookups, cooldown yield at the current PR, uncertain-lookup yield, and the REST-core gate cursor.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-post-merge-review-cursor.sh`: 18 passed, 0 failed.
- `test-gh-secondary-cooldown.sh`, `test-gh-shim.sh`, `test-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh`, `test-pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker-timeout.sh`: passed.
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --base-ref origin/main`: ALL LOCAL CHECKS PASSED. ShellCheck is clean on all 7 files, with no new string literals or complexity/nesting violations. The shfmt advisories are pre-existing lines outside this diff.

## Remaining for #36054

After release and deploy: compare `gh-api-calls.log` attribution and Pulse scanner yield logs in a later comparable REST-core window against the 08:04–08:11Z baseline, then post the residual evidence on #36054.

title: GH#36118: fix(issue-sync): enrich preserves appended sections and skips footer-only rewrites
body:
## Summary

`issue-sync-helper.sh enrich` runs on every `TODO.md` push and rewrites every plan-linked issue body. It erased the sections other writers append after the signature footer: worker-persisted `### Files Scope`, brief repairs, integration evidence and `feedback-route` blocks. It also rewrote unchanged bodies whenever only the footer differed.

Each rewrite changes the terminal-blocker task revision (`{title, body}` hash). Holds were released as `revision_changed` with the brief context they depended on now gone. Workers then blocked again on the missing scope or guidance, which produced repeat dispatches and comment churn. #36061 (t18806) shows the full cycle (evidence in #36118).

## Root cause (corrected from the issue)

- Cases 2 and 3 of `_enrich_update_issue` treated the whole body as issue-sync-owned and wrote the composed body over it.
- The no-op check compared `current_body == composed`. `compose_issue_body` appends its own signature footer with the current framework version, so any release changed the composed body. A body with an appended tail never matched. The issue said compose emits no footer; that was wrong, but the effect is the same.

## Change

`.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper-enrich.sh`:
- `_enrich_body_head`: the issue-sync-owned head — body before `<!-- aidevops:sig -->`, minus the origin marker and trailing blank lines.
- `_enrich_body_tail`: everything after the first signature paragraph.
- `_enrich_dedupe_tail`: drops appended sections whose heading the composed head now declares, so a brief that gains `### Files Scope` never yields two scope sections. Feedback-route blocks and fenced code are carried verbatim.
- `_enrich_carry_tail`: composed body (with its fresh footer) + the deduped tail.
- `_enrich_update_issue`: cases 2/3 skip when heads match. Otherwise they write composed + tail. `FORCE_ENRICH` still always writes, and also carries the tail; this covers the `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` stub force-enrich path. Case 4 (external body) is unchanged. The function stays under the complexity limit by unifying the case 2/3 branch.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-brief-inline-classifier.sh` — 27/27, including new D6 (footer-only → no write), D7 (head change → composed + tail, one signature), D8 (scope dedupe, feedback block kept), D9 (FORCE carries tail).
- `test-enrich-no-data-loss.sh` 13/13, `test-issue-sync-enrich-bounds.sh` 8/8, `test-issue-sync-held-body.sh` 34/34, `test-issue-sync-refresh-body.sh` pass.
- Pre-existing failures that reproduce identically on unchanged `main` at `5cc8e8c1d0`: `test-enrich-dedup-guard.sh` (dry-run parent-task parity), `test-enrich-batch-prefetch.sh` (REST fallback cache), `test-override-flags.sh` section 5 (headless sandbox).
- `shellcheck` clean; `complexity-regression-helper.sh check --metric function-complexity`: base 0, head 0, new 0.
- Live replay against the real #36061 revisions (read-only probe): the 10:26 body vs the 15:03 composed body → **skip** (the erasure would not have happened). A head change → composed + Files Scope / Worker Guidance / Integration evidence / feedback-route start+complete, one signature. Re-running is idempotent.

## Follow-up after deploy

Restore #36061's appended brief from its 10:26 revision so t18806 dispatches with full context. The next `TODO.md` push should log `Body unchanged` for unchanged plan-linked issues.

Resolves #36118
For #36061

title: t18817: fix(terminal-blocker): re-arm must not release holds with unresolved blocked-by dependencies
body:
## Summary

The terminal-blocker re-arm released holds (status:blocked -> status:available) without checking blocked-by dependencies. The dependency normalizer then re-blocked them within minutes, and the posted rearm receipt retired the queue entry, so nothing released the hold once the dependency closed (the dep-graph auto-unblock also defers while a terminal-blocker hold is current). Observed on a managed repo: two holds flipped about 50 times over 17 days without a worker running. _tbr_release_circuit_hold now calls a new _tbr_dependency_unresolved helper (same is_blocked_by_unresolved predicate as stale recovery, lazy-loading pulse-dep-graph.sh, fail-open if the library cannot load) after a revision_changed/trusted_retry decision and before the receipt check. While a dependency is open it logs reason=dependency_blocked and returns 3; _tbr_check_entry keeps the entry and decision and does not stamp rearm_checked_updated_at, so every pass rechecks it and releases once the dependency resolves. Receipt format, trust rules and the dependency normalizer are unchanged.

title: t18819: fix(checkpoint): exact-head approval supersedes a runner's own draft hold-for-review
body:
## Summary

A worker that needed brief-owner input labelled its own draft hold-for-review; the owner's valid exact-head CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_APPROVED could never continue it because _pr_checkpoint_revised_target kept every PR label (#36061/#36070 deadlock). New _pr_checkpoint_self_hold_superseded (pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh) drops only hold-for-review from the local normalized PR view when every labeled hold event was by the approved runner (= PR author) before the approval comment, the issue has no PR-only completion-contract marker or feedback-route automation-hold record for that PR, and the PR has no release-approval-required label; unreadable PR events fail closed. The continuation target row gains a trailing self_hold flag and _pcc_dispatch removes the PR label via gh_pr_edit_safe only after a successful exact-head launch (not on failure or dedup). Prevention: worker-discipline.md outcome C and the post-merge-review-scanner generated issue body now route genuine decisions through BLOCKED input_required with TERMINAL_BLOCKER_INPUT_OWNER=maintainer (revision re-arms dispatch) and forbid self-applied hold-for-review.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/worker-discipline.md, .agents/scripts/post-merge-review-scanner.sh, .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-revision.py

## Decisions

Actor match uses the PR author, so in single-account setups pulse-applied PR holds share the login; the explicit PR-only, feedback-route and release-approval exclusions cover the known same-login PR hold producers (pulse-issue-reconcile and NMR holds label issues, not PRs). Label removal is best-effort and logged: the fence already treats the superseded hold as answered. Scope extension beyond the brief: post-merge-review-scanner.sh carried the same outcome-C self-hold instruction in generated issue bodies; hold-for-review/labeled literals moved to constants to satisfy the string-literal ratchet.

title: GH#36132: cut dispatcher reuse-selection cost in precreate_worktree
body:
## Summary

Measured the precreate_worktree tail from this runner raw records, then optimized the largest measured leaf: dispatcher-side reuse selection (_dlw_select_issue_worktree). The loop forked printf|awk and printf|awk|sed for every listed worktree. It now parses `git worktree list --porcelain` with shell builtins, using the same pattern as get_worktree_path_for_branch in worktree-helper-add.sh.

### Runner-local precondition

`dispatch-stage-instrument.sh report 86400` shows precreate.helper_add n=49 (24 h). `report 259200` shows n=266 (72 h). The raw log covers 2026-10-26 to 2026-10-30. Analysis uses the large repo (a private monorepo with 116 linked worktrees), 72 h window.

### Per-stage table (72 h, large repo, seconds)

| Stage | p50 | p90 | max | n |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| precreate_worktree (total) | 13.2 | 21.9 | 40.5 | 314 |
| precreate.helper_add (wrapper) | 9.7 | 14.8 | 28.0 | 260 |
| precreate.create_worktree (wrapper) | 6.3 | 9.3 | 17.3 | 260 |
| precreate.git_worktree_add | 2.8 | 4.0 | 9.8 | 258 |
| precreate.helper_deps | 1.3 | 2.0 | 4.4 | 227 |
| precreate.restore_deps | 1.0 | 1.8 | 3.5 | 227 |
| precreate.base_fetch | 1.2 | 1.8 | 2.6 | 260 |
| precreate.verify_generation | 1.0 | 1.7 | 3.4 | 227 |
| precreate.managed_enroll | 0.3 | 0.7 | 2.6 | 227 |
| precreate.registry_register | 0.3 | 0.6 | 2.3 | 258 |
| precreate.sibling_status | 0.2 | 0.5 | 1.3 | 260 |
| stale/unmerged remote checks | 0.2 | 0.4 | 0.7 | 260 |

Derived from raw attempts. Helper-side records were joined to helper_add by issue and start_ns inside the window; n=260.

| Unrecorded interval | p50 | p90 | max |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| dispatcher reuse selection (precreate_worktree start to helper_add start) | 2.8 | 5.2 | 8.9 |
| dispatcher registration (helper_add end to precreate_worktree end, minus restore_deps) | 0.8 | 1.6 | 3.1 |
| helper startup (helper_add start to capacity_check) | 0.8 | 1.3 | 2.3 |
| base-ref resolution gap inside create_worktree | 0.7 | 1.1 | 2.0 |

Over the full log (n=475), reuse selection was p50 2.9 / p90 6.3 / max 23.9 s. That is the largest single leaf at p90; git_worktree_add was 4.5 s at p90.

### Concurrency grouping (full log, overlapping same-repo helper_add attempts)

- git_worktree_add p50 by overlap level: 1: 2.9 s (n=392), 2: 2.9 s (n=50), 3: 3.0 s (n=20).
- base_fetch: 1: 1.3 s, 2: 1.1 s.

Same-repo object-store contention is ruled out on this host. The slowest cluster (5 attempts at 2026-10-27 14:13Z, helper_add 33 to 45 s) inflated every sub-stage by the same factor, including python verify and deps. That pattern indicates host-wide load, not a serialized git resource. A per-repo creation lock or a shared fetch would therefore add latency, not remove it.

This runner does not reproduce the 142.5 s maintainer-host baseline: its total p90 is 21.9 s. The fix targets the dominant stage measured here. It also applies on the maintainer host, where precreate_worktree p50 minus helper_add p50 is about 3.4 s and the host has 30+ worktrees.

### Out of scope, filed separately

Raw records show 35 worktree_precreation_failed in 24 h on this runner. Root cause: GH#35996 generation enrollment refuses group-writable git admin dirs created under umask 002. Filed as #36142 with reproduction. That issue also covers the managed-precreation case in test-precreation-failure-skip.sh, which already fails on main.

No CPU/idle/core-count gating. No change to the prelaunch deadline, publication reserve, lease TTL or orphan grace.

.agents/reference/dispatch-timing.md, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-systemd.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-precreation-failure-skip.sh

- found branch: 2735 ms -> 271 ms
- absent: 2439 ms -> 272 ms
- absent: 2852 ms -> 291 ms
Identical rc/path/branch/refusal results. Also identical on the aidevops canonical repo (1.2-1.4 s -> 0.27-0.34 s).

Checks:

- test-prelaunch-publication-reserve.sh: 6/6.

title: GH#36169: fix compaction effort, credential-aware compaction routing, simple tier high
body:
## Summary

Fixes three compaction routing defects and raises the simple-tier reasoning level.

1. **Compaction effort was never applied.** OpenCode v1.19.5 builds compaction request options from the **parent user message's variant** (`session/llm/request.ts`) and ignores `agent.compaction.variant`. A Luna compaction under an Opus `max` or Sol `xhigh` parent therefore ran at the provider default. Stored compactions confirm this: rows tagged `max`/`xhigh` show only ~20–350 reasoning tokens. `applyCompactionEffort` (`compaction-effort.mjs`, called from `chat.params`) now merges the compaction model's own catalogued variant options for one fixed target. The target is `settings.compaction_reasoning` (default `high`, accepted `medium`..`max`), with `AIDEVOPS_COMPACTION_EFFORT` as an override and the legacy `AIDEVOPS_COMPACTION_MAX_EFFORT` as a cap. When the model has no variant for the target, it falls back to the highest catalogued variant below it; Luna's highest is `xhigh`.
2. **No OpenAI credentials meant broken compaction.** The plugin always registers `config.provider.openai`, so an uncredentialed Luna route failed with "OpenAI API key is missing". Candidates now need stored auth, an env key or credential options. Without OpenAI credentials, Haiku 5.5 (1M context, native catalog, managed-limit fallback) compacts. With no usable candidate, compaction stays on the parent model.
3. **Stale docs.** Removed the obsolete "Haiku's 168K" note (Haiku 5.5 has 1M context) and documented how compaction effort actually works.
4. **Simple tier → `high`.** Luna and Haiku 5.5 both cost $0.10/$0.50 per 1M tokens, so the extra reasoning is nearly free (user request). `max` is not used because Luna has no `max` variant.

`gpt-6.1-luna` does not exist in the catalog (checked 2026-10-31). Luna stays pinned at `gpt-6-luna`.

## Replay evidence

Two real interactive compaction points (71K and 75K input) were replayed through `opencode serve` with this branch's plugin. Each run forked the session at the original compaction trigger, ran summarize, then deleted the fork.

| Config | secs (A / B) | reasoning tokens (A / B) | output tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| Luna medium | 21.7 / 22.2 | 69 / 108 | ~3.0K |
| Luna high | 23.4 / 27.2 | 639 / 587 | ~2.6K |
| Luna xhigh | 50.0 / 60.3 | 4055 / 4518 | ~2.5K |
| Haiku 5.5 high | 88.7 / 102.8 | 14755 / 15897 | 5.6K / 8.6K |

- Reasoning tokens rise with the configured effort, so the hook works end to end.
- A blinded fact-retention comparison found **no monotonic retention gain from medium → high → xhigh on Luna**. Higher effort traded details rather than adding them. `xhigh` handled one in-flight retry state better, and `high` misreported it once.
- Haiku high kept the broadest context in both cases but took 4x as long. In each case it also dropped or reopened one consequential item (a completed operation result; release authority).
- Decision: keep Luna first, use `high` as the default compaction effort (small latency cost, recovers reasoning that was previously lost), and keep Haiku as the no-OpenAI fallback. OpenCode reads the compaction model from global config only, so it cannot be switched per parent provider.

## Verification

- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/`: 1261 pass, 0 fail, 7 skipped (at `dc57f6855c`)
- `qlty-regression-helper.sh --base 7ee6465fa6 --head dc57f6855c`: 34 → 34, no regression. The effort logic moved to `compaction-effort.mjs` so `compaction-routing.mjs` no longer trips `qlty:file-complexity`.
- `node --test .agents/scripts/tests/test-model-ab-helper.mjs`: pass
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-model-routing-overlay.sh`: PASS
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-variant.sh`: all pass
- Live replay above, run with both OpenAI and Anthropic OAuth credentials

Resolves #36169

title: t18821: fix(worker): re-verify and defer unreadable POST_PR_HANDOFF instead of tier escalation
body:
## Summary

A GitHub read failure or local transport deferral (quota cooldown/pacing, exit 75) made the exact-head handoff probe return unknown. _worker_produced_output fails that open to pr_exists, the same class it prints for a confirmed ready PR, and _hrw_handle_unverified_post_pr_handoff routed every such class to claim release + fast-fail(overwhelmed) + cascade tier escalation. Observed: 10 of 21 post_pr_handoff outcomes in 24h were worker_post_pr_handoff_unverified, e.g. #36081/PR #36091 escalated to tier:thinking 13s after the wrapper's deferred read, then merged by Pulse 26 min later. Fix: _worker_post_pr_handoff_confirmed records the observed state in _WORKER_POST_PR_HANDOFF_STATE (rejected/unknown/merged_issue_unreadable/merged_issue_open/raw probe state). The handler re-verifies up to AIDEVOPS_POST_PR_HANDOFF_VERIFY_ATTEMPTS (default 3) every AIDEVOPS_POST_PR_HANDOFF_VERIFY_DELAY_SECONDS (default 20) only when the state was unreadable, or when the classifier readback (pr_exists) disagrees with a strict missing-linkage/summary result. Confirmed on retry -> normal verified success path. Still unreadable -> worker_post_pr_handoff_verification_deferred: deferred terminal outcome, claim retained, no CLAIM_RELEASED, no fast-fail, no escalation. Identity rejections and consistent definitive states keep the existing failure path. The failure log line now includes output_class and handoff_state. The gate moved into _hrw_post_pr_handoff_gate so _hrw_finish_success_run stays under the 100-line complexity limit. Also isolates test-headless-runtime-release-unlock.sh blocker telemetry via AIDEVOPS_WORKER_BLOCKER_LOG_FILE in its temp dir; 7 owner/repo SECOND_CONFIG fixture rows had leaked into the live worker-progress-blockers.jsonl.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-checkpoint-tests.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-release-unlock.sh, TODO.md

## Decisions

Deferred (not success) preserves the GH#33115 invariant that an unverifiable handoff is never counted as completion. Retaining the claim mirrors the existing inconclusive-PR path; the pushed PR stays the dedup signal, and stale-claim recovery or Pulse merge decide on fresh state. The bounded wrapper wait (about 40s by default) bridges short cooldowns; longer cooldowns take the deferred route rather than holding the slot. Linkage/summary read failures inside the shared _pr_handoff_state_for_branch_or_issue still classify as missing_*; the disagreement check covers that case for this caller, and changing the shared probe would affect other callers, so it is out of scope.

## Runtime Testing

- **Verification:** runtime-verified — runtime-verified: real helper functions run against merged PR #36091 / closed issue #36081 in a scratch worktree on the PR's exact branch and head e4803885 with origin remote and origin/main fetched (1 commit ahead, remote branch deleted, as after a real merge); only GitHub writes (claim release, fast-fail, status edits) were stubbed. (3) GitHub readable, fixed helper: definitive merged_missing_summary (PR genuinely has 0 MERGE_SUMMARY comments) on both probes, existing failure path immediately, no re-verify wait. title: t18822: fix(pulse): rerun orphaned in_progress jobs on GitHub-hosted runners
body:
## Summary

GH#35538 added _sq_orphan_job_run to rerun a concluded workflow run whose job record is stuck in_progress, but it required the job's runner to be listed by GET repos/{repo}/actions/runners as online and busy=false. That endpoint lists self-hosted runners only, so a GitHub-hosted orphan could never qualify and its PR stayed pending forever. Observed on worker PR #36110: run 41108813201 (Qlty Regression Gate) completed/failure at 2026-10-30T18:43Z while job 'Detect PR scope' stayed in_progress (runner 'GitHub Actions 1001493429', runner_group_id 0, runner_group_name 'GitHub Actions') and two dependent jobs stayed queued; the repo has 0 self-hosted runners, so the PR sat 7.5h with 3 pending checks and Pulse could neither merge nor repair it. Fix: new _sq_orphan_runner_released accepts a GitHub-hosted job (runner_group_id 0 and runner_group_name 'GitHub Actions', read from the already-fetched job JSON) without the runner lookup, and keeps the online/idle proof for self-hosted runners. All other guards are unchanged: completed_at null, started before the orphan cutoff (default 2h), run conclusion non-null, one rerun per run ID persisted before the write, at most 5 reruns per repo scan, check conclusions never altered. reference/github-runner-stale-queued-watchdog.md documents both runner cases.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/github-runner-stale-queued-watchdog.md, .agents/scripts/pulse-stale-queued-runs.sh, TODO.md

## Decisions

Hosted identification uses both runner_group_id 0 and runner_group_name 'GitHub Actions', so custom and self-hosted runner groups keep the idle-runner proof. A concluded run whose hosted job is still listed in_progress after 2h cannot be executing, because hosted runners are ephemeral and a run concludes only after its jobs finish; the existing once-per-run marker bounds any misjudgement to a single rerun. No new test fixture: the real-run verification covers the hosted path and the existing fixture covers the self-hosted path.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — runtime-verified: called _sq_orphan_job_run on the real stuck job (repo marcusquinn/aidevops, PR #36110, job 124245544865, run 41108813201). title: t18804: record quota-series metadata on production REST rows (GH#36054)
body:
## Summary

For #36054 (t18804). This is a partial delivery and the issue stays open. It keeps the instrumentation from PR #36049 and adds the missing production link.

**Root cause:** the default REST governor path (`_gh_transport_run_rest` → `gh_record_attempt`) already sees the reset epoch, the cumulative `x-ratelimit-used` and the credential, but it dropped all three. Production rows never formed (pool, credential, reset) series. On this host the report showed `missing_metadata_attempts: 81678` and `series: []`.

**Change:**
- `gh_native_response.py`: response metadata now includes `used` (`x-ratelimit-used`).
- `gh-transport-governor.py`: emits `auth_fingerprint` and `sampled_at`. The fingerprint is a sha256 of host + `\x1f` + token, the same digest as `_ghqa_auth_fingerprint`. The token is never written.
- `gh-transport-controls.sh`: passes fingerprint, reset, sample time and `used` to `gh_record_attempt` (fields 20–22 and 7).
- `gh-api-aggregate.awk`: rows where the credential is known but the reset is not (for example native rows without headers) go into `same_credential_reset_unknown_cost`. This value is shown next to the residual and never subtracted. Old rows without metadata still count in `missing_metadata_attempts`.

## Investigation (live, read-only)

A sampler polled `GET /rate_limit` (free) every ~2 s for the host default credential (digest prefix `2c37be71b4fc`). It also took 0.2 s snapshots of native `gh`/`curl` processes with owner and parent.

| Window (UTC, one reset epoch) | sampled `used` delta | local logged cost | residual |
|---|---|---|---|
| 02:47:38–02:51:52 | 221 | 33 | 188 (85.1%) |
| 02:52:42–02:59:32 | 413 | 131 | 282 (68.3%) |

**Majority consumer (window 2):**
- Local coverage is close to complete. The sampler saw 694 native `gh` children under `gh-transport-governor.py`, against 733 logged governor rows. The only same-OS-user native `gh` processes that bypass the shim were 12 `gh send-telemetry` (no REST cost), 1 `gh api user` and 1 `gh auth git-credential`.
- Dispatch claims show **two active runner devices for the same login**: this host and `device-1791380361-…`, which is not on this host. That device posted an ops comment on #36174 at 02:56:02Z, inside the window. REST-core limits are per user, so its calls drain the same bucket but are invisible to this host's log.
- The other OS user on this host runs as a different login, so it uses a separate bucket. It is excluded.
- Conclusion: the residual is most consistent with the second same-login device. This is an inference, not a measurement; proof needs that device's log for the same (digest, reset) window.
- Narrow follow-up filed: #36187 (t18825). It labels this cost as `same_login_external_cost` in the series output.

**Reduction not yet shown:** the deployed runtime still writes pre-change rows (no digest/reset), so a later window with fewer unattributed rows needs this PR deployed first. The drop from 85.1% to 68.3% between windows comes from workload variation, not this change.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-api-instrument.sh`: 268 passed, 0 failed (includes the new reset-unknown assertions).
- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py`: 68 OK.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim.sh`: `Results: 173 passed, 3 failed`. Test 27, including the new "REST transport records credential digest, reset epoch and used counter" check, passes. Test 26 has 3 failures (`manual/automatic dispatch-intent issue edit`, `issue-edit dispatch conflict normalization`). An unmodified `origin/main` tree shows the same 3 failures: `Results: 172 passed, 3 failed`. They come from the environment and existed before this change; this PR does not touch them.
- Qlty: the first head (`502776a80`) took `gh-transport-governor.py` to total complexity 50 (+1 file-complexity smell). `aa33df563` removes the redundant anonymous guard: `run()` already rejects unauthenticated identities before the digest is computed. A local `qlty smells` run now reports no smell for that file.
- `shellcheck` is clean on the touched shell files. `python3 -m py_compile` is OK on both .py files. `git diff --check` is clean.
- Live: `.agents/scripts/gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops` through the worktree shim wrote a row with digest `2c37be71b4fc…`, reset `1793415577` and used `3764`.
- The pre-push `bun run typecheck` could not start locally (`tsc` is missing); this is left to CI. No TypeScript was touched.

title: t18823: fix(release): retry indeterminate repo-state authority instead of silently dropping CLAIM_RELEASED
body:
## Summary

Root cause of stranded worker claims such as #35977 / draft #35984: aidevops_can_manage_repo_issue_state returned 1 both for a confirmed read/none verdict and for an unanswered lookup, and _release_dispatch_claim treated 1 as a benign no-op. At 2026-10-30T16:39Z the REST core transport governor deferred `gh api user` (gh-api-calls.log: account lookup rest-core-selected then transport-deferred), so the repo owner's release logged 'repo state is not managed by this account', posted no CLAIM_RELEASED and left the issue status:in-progress + assigned for 10+ hours; every recovery path then skipped it. Fix: (1) the guard falls back to a live GraphQL viewer login/viewerPermission (separate quota bucket; gh-transport-governor treats graphql as an unsupported shape, so it is not REST-admitted), trusted only when the viewer equals the checked login; (2) the guard returns 2 for indeterminate, 1 only for a confirmed verdict, all callers still fail closed; (3) the release path retries an indeterminate verdict (AIDEVOPS_RELEASE_AUTHORITY_RETRY_DELAYS, default '15 45') and then reports the release unpersisted (rc 1) with an explicit warning instead of a false 'not managed'. Crash/kill-stranded drafts are covered separately by worker-ready #36186; the same REST-only identity class across ~90 `gh api user` call sites is #36192.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh, .agents/scripts/shared-repo-state-guard.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-repo-state-guard.sh, TODO.md

## Decisions

Kept the REST lookup first and uncached (#aidevops:trust-boundary in shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh); GraphQL is a live fallback, not a cache. viewerPermission describes the credential, so it is only trusted when viewer.login equals the login being checked (case-insensitive). Return code 2 changes no caller semantics except the release path, because every other caller uses `if !` / `|| return 1`. aidevops_can_run_repo_routines is unchanged (routines failing closed is harmless).

title: t18827: fix(gh): pace REST admissions as time-to-reset divided by remaining quota
body:
## Summary

GitHub REST core quota (one PAT) was exhausted twice on 2026-10-31. Local
primary pacing exempted the first half of each window, and below half it paced
only when the last 60 s of demand would exhaust the window. Bursts could
therefore spend 2,500+ points unpaced.

`primary_wait()` now uses an even, GCRA-style schedule:

- interval = seconds until `x-ratelimit-reset` / (`x-ratelimit-remaining` - in-flight reservations)
- `pacing.retry_at` stores the next on-schedule slot; each admission advances it by one interval
- up to 10 admissions may run ahead at full quota; the allowance scales down with the remaining share, so scarce windows are spaced strictly
- the returned deferral time solves `t = slot - ahead * (reset - t) / available`, so callers are not re-deferred by the shrinking interval
- the final-point exemption, the serialized stale-refresh path, cooldowns, and the 100-concurrent / 900-points-per-minute secondary ceilings are unchanged

Server-reported `remaining` already counts spend by ungoverned commands (such
as `gh pr checks --watch` and `gh run watch`) and by other hosts on the same
credential. The interval therefore tightens automatically when that spend
drains the window.

## Evidence

Replay simulation using the real `Budget` admission path: 3 req/s offered
governed demand over a 3,600 s / 5,000-point window.

| Scenario | Old code | New code |
|----------|----------|----------|
| Governed only, remaining at 15 / 30 / 45 / 59 min | — | 3,732 / 2,478 / 1,230 / 89; 4,999 used by reset |
| Plus 0.5 req/s ungoverned, remaining at 15 / 30 / 45 min | 2,263 / 1,191 / 296; zero by ~min 52 | 3,343 / 1,853 / 604; zero only in the final minutes |

Ungoverned pollers alone spend about 1,800 points per hour. Moving them
under governance is noted as a follow-up in #36199.

## Verification

- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py`: 68 tests OK. Pacing tests that encoded the healthy-half exemption were rewritten for even spacing, burst bound, scarce-window spacing and a long-window saved slot. Two debt-accounting tests now use high-quota headers so they stay independent of pacing.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim.sh`: Test 27 (transport controls and response-owned quota) all pass. 3 failures in Test 26 are in the shell dispatch-label normalization for `issue edit`, which does not route through the Python governor and is untouched by this diff.
- `qlty check` on changed files: no issues.

Resolves #36199

- `.agents/services/email/ses.md` "IAM Policy": new "Workload send-only policy" subsection. title: t18830: fix(dispatch): bound pre-launch abort loops with a self-healing windowed backoff
body:
## Summary

Pre-launch dispatch aborts looped forever across runners (#36061: five alternating attempts in an hour, each leaving one `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=prelaunch` comment and nothing else). The zero-attempt fuse never saw them, ignored peer runners on user-owned repos, and when it did trip it applied a permanent `status:blocked` that needed a human requeue.

This replaces that fuse with a self-healing, windowed backoff evaluated **before** any claim is posted.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-prompt.sh`
  - Orphan `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=prelaunch` comments count as zero-attempt evidence, once per author+token. Conditions: token/device/session present, older than `DISPATCH_CLAIM_ORPHAN_GRACE`, no surviving claim for the token, and no same-author `ready`/`terminal`/`Dispatching worker` for it.
  - `_dlw_evidence_trusted_authors` resolves ambiguous COLLABORATOR/CONTRIBUTOR/NONE evidence authors with `_gh_actor_has_repo_write_authority`. Only write/maintain/admin counts, a failed lookup fails closed, and at most 5 lookups run per snapshot (`#aidevops:trust-boundary`). Reset authority stays OWNER/MEMBER.
  - Metrics TSV gains: windowed evidence count, windowed notice count, evidence epochs, latest authoritative reset epoch.
  - `_dlw_hold_repeated_zero_output` holds while windowed evidence (`ZERO_OUTPUT_HOLD_WINDOW_SECONDS`, default 43200) reaches the threshold. It changes no labels, posts at most one `dispatch-infrastructure-failure` notice per window with an estimated resume time, and logs `DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=zero_attempt_backoff`. The local fast-fail counter follows the same window and maintainer reset.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh`: `_dispatch_dedup_check_layers` runs the backoff after the capacity, state-label and dependency gates and before `check_dispatch_dedup` can write a claim. It returns benign rc 3. Peer commit 618f9f1b87 moved it here so ineligible candidates never fetch evidence or post a notice.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`: `_dlw_preclaim_zero_attempt_backoff` shares one metrics snapshot with prompt preparation. Direct `_dispatch_launch_worker` callers evaluate it before the prelaunch lease. The post-lease hold call is gone.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`, `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`: `zero_attempt_backoff` is a benign block reason with the terminal-backoff negative-cache TTL.
- `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md`: documents the new backoff.

## Verification

- `test-pulse-dispatch-worker-launch-comment-metrics.sh`: all pass. New cases cover orphan leases once per write-verified author+token, a read/triage collaborator and a failed lookup not counting, one notice per window, age-out self-heal, and the shared pre-claim snapshot.
- `test-zero-output-url-fallback.sh`: 17/17. The hold assertions now check the windowed contract (no relabel). New cases cover aged local state self-healing and a maintainer reset releasing local state.
- `test-precreation-failure-skip.sh`: 59/59. Covers benign rc 3, no claim and no prelaunch lease while held.
- `test-prelaunch-publication-reserve.sh`: 6/6.
- 21 other dispatch tests that source these modules pass. After the peer commit, 14 suites were re-run and all pass, including `test-pulse-dispatch-core-external-author-gate.sh`, `test-pre-dispatch-validator.sh` and `test-dispatch-dedup-gh-call-budget.sh`. `test-pulse-wrapper-worker-detection.sh` fails 1 case (`dispatch_max ... empty-snapshot login`, login_calls=2). It fails the same way on unmodified `origin/main`, so this PR did not cause it.
- ShellCheck is clean on all changed scripts. The complexity guard reports no new violations.

Post-deploy check (from the brief): #36061 should gain no new orphan prelaunch leases while held, and `pulse.log` should show `DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=zero_attempt_backoff` for it.

Resolves #36214

title: feat: add registry-authorized worktree retirement and preservation
body:
## Summary

Make controlled worktree retirement depend on the lifecycle registry rather than legacy ownership records, process-CWD snapshots, branch reachability, or PR status.

- Record controlled creation and admit runtime-identified owners before writes. Independent launches receive their own admission attempt; closed generations and reused paths cannot redirect queued work.
- Retire only after registered owners end and admission closes atomically. Journal preservation, relocation, and removal so interrupted operations remain retryable without deleting replacement directories.
- Preserve commits, staged/unstaged changes, and ordinary untracked files in verified Git-only archives. Ignored files remain deliberately excluded. Preserve symlink metadata consistently across Linux/macOS and avoid refreshing the source Git index during fingerprinting.
- Route manual and Pulse worktree-removal entrypoints through registry retirement without a legacy fallback.

## Linked issue

Ref #35996 — extends the completed generation-enrollment/admission work with controlled creation, verified preservation, and retirement. This is a follow-up, not a request to reopen that issue.

## Implementation and review scope

- Core: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/{creation,session,cleanup_plan,preservation,retirement,cleanup}.py`, with existing admission/enrollment/launch integration.
- Consumers: `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-state.sh`, `worktree-helper-cmds.sh`, the Pulse removal helpers, CodeGraph/headless launchers, and `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/` admission hooks.
- Filesystem preservation: `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_*.py` and `worktree_retirement_filesystem.py`; reuse the existing archive verification and native Git removal paths.
- Contract, verification evidence, and limitations: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/CLEANUP.md`, `COMPATIBILITY.md`, and the two registry reports. There remain four reports total: process/registry on Linux/macOS.

## Runtime Testing

- [x] `runtime-verified` — disposable native Git/process/filesystem paths and the portable validator were exercised; production rollout is not claimed.

### Current head `27df42f11`

- Rebased and squashed onto upstream `7cc4fec50`: one feature commit, retaining upstream bounded Git packing, missing-promisor-base recovery, and fingerprint module extraction.
- Resolved archive conflicts without weakening symlink preservation: Git-only link targets remain portable; tar-preserved untracked links retain verified mode metadata. Added the extracted fingerprint/base-source modules to the portable bundle allowlist.
- Full Linux lifecycle suite rerun: **163/163** in 511.508 seconds. Rebuilt portable registry bundle: **101/101**, zero failures/errors/skips, SHA-256 `08706fca4fe8e84bde4658798aff8d6e4164aad4fc6ea3f8bc0ef917f6728c49`. Production/bundle sources are unchanged by the final test-only amendment. Scoped Ruff 0.11.13 and diff checks passed; fresh macOS validation remains pending.
- The broad archive suite exceeded its 20-minute budget; no full-suite pass is claimed. Its three observed failures were obsolete expectations that legacy archives permit source deletion. Updated the Pulse, manual `--force`, and interrupted-scratch consumer tests to assert refusal and retained source data; the focused rerun passed **3/3**. Archive restoration and owned verification-scratch recovery remain exercised without granting source-removal authority. Symlink-mode/Darwin metadata regressions also passed **4/4**.
- Required CI and review gate passed on `f23d0ec6f`; final test-only head `27df42f11` requires fresh CI. The guarded merge helper independently refuses this fork PR because its contextual `Ref #35996` is not a closing-linked issue; no authority bypass was used.

### Previous head `ee6c9c2bb` verification

- Full Linux lifecycle suite: **163/163** in 523.783 seconds, including creation, admission, preservation, retirement, private-group/ACL enrollment, and interruption/retry cases.
- Targeted OpenCode Git safety, signature, output-compaction, and TUI suites with Python 3.9: **123/123**. Lifecycle admission now precedes signature-footer mutation. Interpreter compatibility uses `Path.lstat()` rather than the newer `stat(follow_symlinks=False)` API.
- Worktree-removal audit: **72/72**; Pulse temporary cleanup: **14/14**; Python Git guard adapter: **14/14**. Profile-boundary checks require legacy recovery cleanup to retain the source/archive without registry authority.
- Native managed-runner suite: **10/10**, including actual user-systemd creation/retirement and caller umask. Producers enter the existing native lifecycle launcher before creating worktrees; parent runtime identity is replaced, while explicit generation/attempt admission requirements remain mandatory.
- Full profile-contributions fail-closed suite: **28/28**. This reproduces and fixes the failed CI publication/cleanup path without weakening its success or preservation assertions. Fixtures use private registry state and cwd rather than the invoking session's worktree.
- Profile README boundary suite: **28/28**, after including the native launcher in its isolated helper installation. Managed-runner tests were rerun: **10/10**. Their Bash/Git discovery is portable; fixed argv is reused directly, not read back from subprocess results. Ruff, ShellCheck and targeted Bandit B603/B607 checks passed; only individually audited fixed test commands carry B603 annotations.
- Hook-installation preflight: **31/31**, including global/project installations, missing helpers, help-only helpers and invalid responses. The standalone installer checks the real admission-shaped API in an isolated non-Git directory before changing hooks/settings. Missing dependencies require deploying/repairing the framework first, rather than installing a broken guard. Runtime bundle deployment suite: **70 checks passed**; deployment freshness includes the lifecycle adapter.
- Centralized cleanup: **6/6**, including repeated refusal without allocating legacy archives. Registry eligibility, preservation and retirement now own the complete linked-candidate operation. Launcher/removal contracts: **7/7**; creation fixtures: **2/2**, with system/global Git configuration isolated. Manual refusal explains that the source is retained and force cannot bypass registry checks; rollout and Git-capability documentation corrected.
- Full Qlty regression gate 0.643.0 for head `ee6c9c2bb` against base `1f9679672`: **34 → 34, delta 0**. Documentation passes the Markdown file-size gate. Their blobs match the current upstream default branch. Reproduction, exact files, and a separate implementation brief are recorded in #36273; no production trust policy was relaxed.

The committed portable reports below belong to the earlier bundle, not this head. Rebase preserves upstream enrollment diagnostics, portable Git resolution, and configurable archive Git timeout. Maintainer edits remain disabled.

### Earlier verification, before rebase

- Portable registry validator: **101/101 on Linux and 101/101 on macOS**, zero failures/errors/skips, identical bundle SHA-256: `81799f5e3ced5277f45db81f653ac97ea68987b8481027d3e70c601e3a0bc534`.

- Existing tests cover late writes, Git locks, interrupted retirement, and pathname replacement. No new test runner or infrastructure.

## Risk and boundaries

**Risk: high** — this changes deletion authorization. Unknown or insufficient registry evidence preserves the worktree; `--force` does not override the registry.

The contract requires cooperating, registered writers. These results do not qualify production rollout, real AI-worker/sandbox execution, unregistered writers, power-loss/disk-full/reboot behavior, or actual PID reuse. Legacy candidate selectors can still conservatively retain candidates; this is not an exhaustive audit of arbitrary Git calls. No production cleanup or deployment is performed by this PR submission.

title: t18833: fix(terminal-blocker): re-arm permission_required holds that have no published permission request
body:
## Summary

A permission_required terminal-blocker hold (first observation or repeated circuit) with no published permission request now re-arms once per backoff window instead of waiting forever for a retry. New predicate terminal_blocker_permission_request_evidenced (#aidevops:trust-boundary) keeps the hold while the issue has needs-maintainer-permissions or a trusted worker-permission-helper.sh request marker has no later OWNER/MEMBER signed grant/withdrawal or retry. terminal_blocker_permission_window_expired applies the window, ZERO_OUTPUT_HOLD_WINDOW_SECONDS (default 12h, GH#36214), to terminal_blocker_observation_hold_active, terminal_blocker_circuit_active and _tbr_circuit_blocks_release. _tbr_release_circuit_hold adds decision unevidenced_permission_window and projects status:available through _tbr_project_rearm with the existing hidden receipt. The receipt key binds the evidence event plus the window index, so each window releases at most once; existing decision keys keep their historical hash shape. Mechanical rearm passes record the next window boundary (rearm_after) so unchanged snapshots wake when the window expires. The existing hold-label guard (needs-maintainer-permissions, hold-for-review, no-auto-dispatch, parent-task, ...) is unchanged. Re-arming grants no permission. push/network policy timeouts stay retry-only. worker-diagnostics.md documents the contract.
