title: t18842: fix(pulse-merge): route CI/review repair for worker PRs that use For/Ref (GH#36260)
body:
## Summary

Worker PRs that name their work issue with `For #N` or `Ref #N` instead of a closing keyword were never routed to CI or review repair. The pulse logged "routing to CI fix-worker" and then returned without a diagnostic, on every cycle. PR #36213 (`For #36212`) has had a failing required `Framework Validation` since 09:14Z with no repair attempt. Partial deliveries and checkpoints use `For`/`Ref` on purpose, so this left those PRs open indefinitely.

## Root cause

- `_pmp_stage_required_checks` (`pulse-merge.sh`) passes the target from `_extract_linked_issue`, which reads closing keywords only. For `For #N` PRs that target is empty.
- `_check_pr_merge_gates` does resolve the explicit `For`/`Ref` identity for `origin:worker` PRs, but only into a gate-local variable. That keeps partial work out of post-merge issue closing.
- `_route_pr_resolve_work_issue` (`pulse-merge-process.sh`) resolves `For`/`Ref` only when `kind=conflict` (GH#33763). For `ci` and `review` it calls `_recover_interactive_pr_work_issue`, which returns 1 for any PR not labelled `origin:interactive`. The `|| return 1` then skips `_route_pr_has_linked_issue`, the only step that logs.

Production evidence from the maintainer `pulse.log` at 09:53Z: "worker-briefed auto-merge: PR #36213 … issue #36212, link=non-closing reference", then the CI-drift rebase, then "routing to CI fix-worker". No `_dispatch_ci_fix_worker:` line follows.

## Change

- Non-conflict kinds with no closing target now resolve the work issue with `_extract_pr_work_issue … explicit`. That is the standalone `For`/`Ref` identity the merge gate already trusts, with no title inference. The resolved issue is used only as the repair target, never to close anything.
- When interactive recovery fails, the resolver now continues to the existing "has no linked issue for <kind> repair routing" log instead of returning silently.
- Conflict routing is unchanged. All downstream guards still apply: origin labels, ownership and hold labels, the closed-issue guard, the terminal-route guard, and in-place repair.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh`: clean.
- An ad-hoc harness ran the real `_route_pr_to_fix_worker` and resolvers against `origin/main` and against this branch, with GitHub reads stubbed:

| Case | `origin/main` | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| Worker PR with `For #36212`, ci (the #36213 shape) | rc=1, nothing logged | routed: `kind=ci issue=36212` |
| Worker PR with `For #36212`, review | rc=1, nothing logged | routed: `kind=review issue=36212` |
| Worker PR with no reference | rc=1, nothing logged | rc=1, logs "has no linked issue for ci repair routing" |
| Live interactive PR with `For #42` | rc=1, nothing logged | rc=1, logs "retains active origin:interactive ownership" |
| Ambiguous `For #1` + `Ref #2` | rc=1, nothing logged | rc=1, logs the ambiguity and no linked issue |
| `For` only under a "Related" heading | rc=1, nothing logged | rc=1, logs no linked issue |
| `Resolves #77`, ci | routed, issue 77 | unchanged |
| `For #55`, conflict | routed, issue 55 | unchanged |

- Existing suites all pass:
  - `test-pulse-merge-fix-worker-dispatch.sh`: 52/52
  - `test-pulse-merge-ci-repair-routing.sh`: 79/79
  - `test-pulse-merge-pr-context.sh`: 45/45

  - `test-pulse-merge-superseded-duplicates.sh`: 31/31

  - `test-pulse-merge-closing-contradiction.sh`: rc=0

- Post-deploy check: the next `For`/`Ref` worker PR with terminal CI failures should log `_dispatch_ci_fix_worker:` in `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`.

title: t18844: fix(cloudron-release): reconcile held worker bump PRs in the approval routine
body:
## Summary

Worker release handoffs for Cloudron package bumps could not request maintainer approval while PR checks were pending, so they deferred to automation. The r924 approval routine only processed approval-request issues that already existed. As a result, held bump PRs never reached the maintainer. Their findings stayed assigned and `status:in-review`, and newer findings were deferred behind them. Obsolete bumps stacked up indefinitely: `marcusquinn/aidevops-cloudron-app` had held PRs #225, #233 and #236, no open approval requests, and newest finding #239 deferred.

`release_process` now reconciles held worker PRs after it processes the approval issues (`release_reconcile_held` in `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh`):

- The newest held worker PR that main does not already bundle gets its approval request once its checks are terminal-green. Pending checks wait for the next routine run.
- Older unsigned upstream bumps are superseded: their PRs are closed (branches kept for audit), with their findings and any unsigned approval requests, when main or the requested PR already bundles the upstream.
- Fail-closed boundaries (`#aidevops:trust-boundary`):
  - Signed, stale or unverifiable approvals are never superseded.
  - Human PRs, non-upstream PRs and PRs whose head, labels or state changed since listing are retained.
  - Only OWNER/MEMBER own-line monitor markers identify a finding.
  - API errors stop the process before any write.
- Dry runs (default without `--apply`) never write.

`describe_r924` documents the handoff, and `TODO.md` gains t18844.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh` exits 0. The 8 new held-PR cases cover request/supersede, pending checks, signed approval, unsigned request, dry run, changed PR, untrusted finding marker and API errors.
- Mutation check: disabling the signed-approval guard makes `held: a signed approval is never superseded` fail with an unexpected `pr-close`.
- Review fix (7c74a23859): a trusted linked issue without a monitor marker no longer emits a misaligned finding row; the new regression case fails against the old filter and passes with the fix.
- `shellcheck -x` is clean on the helper, test and `core-routines.sh`. The pre-commit string-literal ratchet passes. `complexity-regression-helper.sh check --base origin/main --working-tree` reports no new violations.
- A read-only dry run against the real package repo reports: request approval for #236; supersede #225 (main already bundles upstream 3.39.75); supersede #233 (#236 bundles the newer v3.39.87).

## Post-merge

After deploy, the next r924 run with `--apply` should leave one pending approval request for #236 and close #225/#233 with their findings. The maintainer still signs with `sudo aidevops approve issue <N> <repo>`; this PR adds no new authority.

Resolves #36268

title: t18845: fix(cloudron-release): provision release approval labels; decouple failed request from supersession
body:
## Summary

Routine r924 (cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh process --apply) has exited 1 on every run since v3.39.104. release_request() created the approval-only issue with --label no-auto-dispatch in a managed package repo that lacks that label, and gh_create_issue intentionally never creates caller-supplied labels (GH#34003). The PR hold labels were already applied, so each run left a half-processed request. The failure also aborted release_reconcile_held() before its supersede loop, so obsolete held bumps that main already bundles were never closed. Fix: (1) managed-label-provisioning-lib.sh gains a canonical release-approval set (release-approval-required, hold-for-review, no-auto-dispatch) and managed_labels_ensure_release_approval_set, following managed_labels_ensure_approval_set (GH#34071 is the same defect class on the edit path). (2) release_request() provisions that set before its first PR label write, replacing the unconditional gh label create --force write; a converged repo costs one label read and no writes; unknown label state fails closed before any hold or issue write. (3) release_held_target() still reports its target when the request fails; release_reconcile_held() counts the failure and continues, so request-independent supersession (main already bundles upstream) proceeds and request-dependent supersession still waits for a real request.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/dispatch-timing.md, .agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/managed-label-provisioning-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-managed-label-provisioning.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t18845-brief.md

title: t18846: fix(pulse-merge): skip partial parent closeout for TODO-projection PRs and closed issues
body:
## Summary

Partial parent closeout (pulse-merge-issue-closeout.sh) treated every `For #N` / `Ref #N` reference in a merged PR body as a delivered slice of a still-open parent. TODO-projection PRs (issue-sync TODO publication and pulse TODO handoff) carry `Ref #N` purely for audit linkage, so each merge posted a false "Partial Parent Closeout" comment, including on issues that were already closed. Those comments are counted as cost receipts by dispatch-dedup-cost.sh, so the noise also skews dispatch decisions.

Changes:
- `_pm_extract_partial_parent_reference` now skips PR bodies carrying `<!-- aidevops:issue-sync-todo-pr -->` or `<!-- aidevops:pulse-todo-handoff id=` in addition to the existing planning-publication marker (GH#36230). A forged marker can only suppress a comment, so marker-only matching is safe.
- `_pm_handle_partial_parent_closeout` reads `.state` from the already-fetched issue JSON and returns before posting when the issue is closed; the comment asserts the parent remains open, which is false for a closed issue.
- Focused coverage in `tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-parent-closeout.sh` for both projection markers, the closed-issue guard, and the open-issue positive path.



## Files Changed

title: GH#36321: bound upstream watch REST cost and serialize retries
body:
## Summary

Bound release summaries to one 10-item listing with metadata from that response; remove per-tag name/date requests. Serialize upstream checks using a stale-PID-recoverable directory lock, persist attempts before execution, and back off for a full hour after failure while retaining the daily success gate.

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/auto-update-freshness-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/upstream-watch-helper-check.sh

## Decisions

Cap every release range at the newest 10 entries, with a visible truncation notice, to guarantee constant network cost even when the old tag is missing. Changes stay within the two issue-scoped files. Independent review findings on Bash 3.2 ownership and long-failure backoff were repaired and runtime-rechecked.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** High
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — ShellCheck and bash -n pass for both changed files; upstream watch mode suite passes 35 cases and issue gate suite passes 18 cases. Focused runtime checks pass concurrent skip, stale PID recovery, immediate failure retry suppression, successful daily gating, state-write failure fail-closed behavior, and missing/found/current tag summaries with exactly two API invocations per range. Repeated runtime checks with BASHPID unset verify fallback lock PID equals the executing check process. A live isolated cmd_check against marcusquinn/aidevops with an absent baseline tag performs four REST endpoint calls (latest release, latest commit, bounded listing, latest release notes) plus gh auth status; gh-api-instrument.sh logs five logical invocations, not an exact quota-cost measurement. Issue publication was disabled only in the temporary verification shell. The unrelated TypeScript typecheck cannot start because tsc dependencies are absent on this runner; pre-push explicitly defers it to CI.

## Regression Evidence

The portable part of this change is the lock-owner PID fallback when `BASHPID` is unavailable. Exercising it needs concurrent background subshells, real sleeps and a forced Bash 3.2 interpreter with the `shared-constants.sh` re-exec guard suppressed (`AIDEVOPS_BASH_REEXECED=1`). The existing upstream-watch suites have no harness for timing-dependent concurrent freshness checks, and adding one would be new test infrastructure. The maintainer interactive session instead ran an out-of-tree runtime harness against the real `check_upstream_watch` and `_show_release_diff` at head `ae72b08983` and again at `27b6b3fe4d`, under both `/bin/bash` 3.2.57 and Homebrew bash 5.3.20, with identical results:

- Two concurrent checks: the watch script ran once, the second check logged "already running — skipping", and the lock was removed afterwards.
- A failed check followed by an immediate re-tick: one run, `last_upstream_watch_attempt` recorded, the second tick was skipped by the 3600 s gate, and no success stamp was written.
- A stale lock owned by dead PID 999999 was recovered and the check ran once.
- `_show_release_diff rtk-ai/rtk no-such-tag-v0 <latest>` (rtk has more than 599 releases) made 2 `gh` calls, showing the 10 newest entries plus a truncation notice. Before this change it made 2 calls per release in the repository's history.

Resolves #36321.

- Read release summary metadata in one bounded listing instead of per-tag lookups or unbounded pagination.
- Serialize upstream freshness checks with a stale-PID-recoverable directory lock.
- Persist attempts before running and enforce a one-hour retry gate after failures.

## Scope

Only `.agents/scripts/upstream-watch-helper-check.sh` and `.agents/scripts/auto-update-freshness-lib.sh` change.

## Verification

ShellCheck and Bash syntax checks pass. Existing upstream watch mode (35 cases) and issue gate (18 cases) suites pass. Focused runtime verification is complete, including concurrent execution, portable PID ownership, failure backoff and a live isolated production check.

The push hook deferred the unrelated TypeScript typecheck to CI because runner dev dependencies (`tsc`) are not installed. No TypeScript files change.
